specs.look: Olive green field jacket, charcoal knit beanie, warm tan skin. Match the Survivor option.
specs.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Production modular player torso sprites for a top-down game. Image 1 is an EXACT geometry/animation layout guide. Image 2 is the approved character design and pixel-art style to apply.
Repaint all 30 torso poses in image 1 as the human character in image 2. CRITICAL: preserve the exact positions, scale, camera, head center, shoulder silhouette, hand centers and arm gestures of each corresponding cell from image 1. The weapon attachment coordinates in game are fixed to those hands; do not move them. Only change appearance and artistic rendering to detailed crisp pixel clusters like image 2. Same healthy human in every frame.
Design: Olive green field jacket, charcoal knit beanie, warm tan skin. Match the Survivor option.
OUTPUT: wide 2:1 PNG, EXACT 8 columns by 4 rows of equal square cells. First 30 cells contain the corresponding torso sprites from reference 1, row-major order; bottom-right two cells empty. The order is all handgun idle/shoot/reload poses, long-gun idle/shoot/reload poses, melee idle/swing poses, then unarmed idle/punch poses, exactly as in image 1. These are TORSO ONLY: head, shoulders, chest, arms and hands. No legs, feet, weapons, bats, guns, armor or backpacks, because those are separate game layers. Hands should retain the gripping poses even though the weapons are absent. Do not add props.
Orthographic directly overhead 90-degree view, facing right; no side or front view. Keep head center and torso pivot fixed within each cell. Full limb silhouettes and generous clear padding. Dark pixel outlines and restrained shaded pixel palette, no painterly blur. Background must be true transparent alpha zero. Remove reference shadows, haze or grey halos; no cast shadows, no white background, no checkerboard, no labels, no borders, no text.
